question: Which Indian institution has developed an affordable device that is capable of rapidly separating plasma from blood and purifying water, priced at ₹1,000?
solution:
The correct answer is __**IIIT-Allahabad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• Researchers at the Indian Institute of** Information Technology, Allahabad (IIIT-A)** developed a **low-cost microfluidic device that separates plasma from whole blood** within minutes using a **hydrodynamic micro-channel design**.
 
• The device also performs **rapid water purification** (removing suspended particles and bacteria) using the same microchannel principles, producing ~one drop of purified fluid per second in prototype tests. 
 
• Cost advantage: the team reports an expected manufacturing price of about** ₹1,000 for the basic unit**—orders of magnitude cheaper than conventional centrifuges and many commercial water-purification systems—making it suitable for rural clinics and field use. 
 
• Technology & recognition: the work (led by **Dr. Amit Prabhakar** and students) was funded by India’s DST, published in a **Royal Society of Chemistry journal** and granted patent protection (20-year patent filings reported).
